source_text.body:
Build a Tidal playlist from your tastes with a browser agent
A user had Comet create a Tidal playlist based on their tastes and named songs; it added songs after back-and-forth but fell short of the requested 50 tracks.
·
Jan 1, 2024
Done with
PC
Perplexity Comet
What they did
A commenter said they opened Tidal and told Comet to inspect their Liked playlist, make a new playlist called Perplexity, and fill it with 50 songs matching their taste plus a few named tracks. After Comet first produced a playlist with one song, the person manually explained the site workflow—search, switch to tracks, and use the plus button—and then prompted it again in smaller batches when it stalled.
How it went
It eventually built a playlist the user liked, mixing familiar songs with new ones, and sometimes asked whether to keep the same categories or add more indie or French music. But it never completed the original 50-song request reliably, often stopping after 2 or 10 additions.
Worth knowing
The main catch was supervision: it only started working after the user taught it the exact Tidal steps, and they still had to keep nudging it with requests like add 10 more.
Try it yourself
with
Perplexity Comet
Copy prompt
Open my [Tidal/Spotify] account and build a playlist called [playlist name] with [number] tracks based on my tastes. I like [artists, songs, genres, moods], and I want it to suit [occasion or activity]. Before adding tracks, show me the proposed list so I can approve or swap songs. Then add them and keep going until the playlist reaches [number] tracks, and tell me the final count.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/perplexity_ai/comments/1m789pe/comet_not_cometing
